chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, altogether from Ibn Mahbub, from Ibn Ri'ab, from Abu Ubayda, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
When you shoot at it with the mi'rad (blunt arrow) and it pierces, then eat; but if it does not pierce and falls sideways, then do not eat.

key_terms.اعْتَرَضَ: Fell sideways/crosswise — indicating the prey was struck by the flat side of the weapon, not killed by penetration, rendering it impermissible
key_terms.المِعْرَاض: A blunt or crossbow-type arrow that kills by its weight and impact rather than by cutting; its use in hunting makes the prey conditionally permissible depending on how it strikes
key_terms.خَرَقَ: To pierce or penetrate — the condition for permissibility when hunting with a blunt weapon

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to eat prey hunted with a blunt arrow (mi'rad) in Islamic law?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) provides a jurisprudential ruling regarding hunting with the mi'rad, a type of blunt or flat-headed arrow that kills by impact rather than penetration. The ruling distinguishes between cases where the prey is pierced (permissible to eat) and where it is merely struck and falls (impermissible). This reflects the classical Shia jurisprudential principle that the manner of slaughter or killing determines the permissibility of consuming the meat.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Abu Ubeyda, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘When you shoot at it with the blunt weapon, so it pierces, so eat; and if it does not pierce, and it turns sideways, so do not eat’.
en.sarwar: 3. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad all from ibn Mahbub from ibn Ri’ab from abu ‘ Ubaydah who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
If you shoot the prey with flareless arrow and if it pierces into the prey you can use it for food; but if it does not pierce into the prey and hits it widthwise, then do not use it for food.”’
